question: Ramu invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Ramu got ₹127.5 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the direct ratio relation between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) is:

⇒ CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200

⇒ 127.5 ÷ SI = (200 + 4) ÷ 200 = 204 ÷ 200 = 51 ÷ 50

⇒ SI = (127.5 × 50) ÷ 51 = 2.5 × 50 = ₹125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹127.5
